correctness.rationale: A maximal independent set with point set S must select exactly the lines disjoint from S, and their union must cover the complement of S. I independently generated PG(2,4) lines as the five-point projective spans of pairs of homogeneous points, checking the incidence degrees and intersections. I enumerated distinct line unions by starting at zero and closing under adjoining any line. A union U yields exactly the maximal independent set with point set P minus U and with all lines contained in U; conversely U is recoverable from every maximal independent set. This calculation enumerated 25,237 distinct unions and reproduced every coefficient in the 17-entry TSV. The size histogram was 8:105, 10:16800, 11:5460, 12:2408, 14:420, 17:42, 21:2. The empty and full unions give the two pure-shore sets. This checks the labeled census without executing the supplied programs or relying on untested larger orders.
residual_risks: Exact finite computation, not a formula for general plane order; no formal proof certification claimed.

value.rationale: The point–line bidegree is a natural refinement on the first square-order projective plane. The exact distribution exposes actual forbidden sizes and balanced versus skew maximal sets, and supplies a reproducible finite benchmark for independent-domination counting in planes. This is stronger than either the known minimum or the existence of a few canonical families.
residual_risks: Finite benchmark only; no quantitative prediction at other orders or asymptotic progress is asserted.
